_comment: Gesture vocabulary for presenter_01.mp4. Each entry names a time window in
that clip which contains one recognisable gesture, so the compositor can pick
a gesture to match what is being said instead of looping the take blindly.
Windows were located by hand-motion energy (scripts/segment_gestures.py) and
then named by eye - motion analysis can tell a still pose from a moving one,
but it cannot tell an open palm from a raised finger.
'role' is what the scheduler matches on, not the key. Keep the three roles
below populated for any new avatar and no scheduling code has to change:
neutral  - resting pose, used whenever nothing else applies
present  - open, explanatory gesture, used on core facts
stress   - tighter, more emphatic gesture, used on deadline scenes
Windows are played ping-pong (forward then reversed) rather than looped, so
they always return to their opening pose and never jump. That also makes a
gesture read as stroke-then-retraction, which is how a real one is shaped.

clasped_rest.note: hands clasped on the desk, minimal motion; the long calm passage

open_palms.note: both hands open wide, palms up - the 'here is the thing' gesture

raised_together.note: hands raised and close together, more insistent
